'''Netsch:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Jim Edgar]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Jim Edgar]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 50.77% {{decrease}} 3.23 [[Percentage point|pp]] }} {{ElectionsIL}} The '''1994 Illinois gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994. Incumbent Republican Governor [[Jim Edgar]] won reelection in a landslide. Edgar carried 101 of the state's 102 counties over the Democratic nominee, [[Illinois Comptroller|State Comptroller]] [[Dawn Clark Netsch]], with Netsch only winning [[Gallatin County, Illinois|Gallatin County]] by a narrow margin. This was the first time in Illinois that a woman was a major party's nominee for governor, with [[2006 Illinois gubernatorial election|2006]] being the only other time. To date, this is the most recent statewide election in which [[Cook County, Illinois|Cook County]] voted for a Republican candidate, a Republican governor won a second term in Illinois, and the last time any gubernatorial candidate received over 60% of the vote. Clark Netsch's 34% of the vote was the worst performance for a Democratic gubernatorial nominee [[1904 Illinois gubernatorial election|in almost a century]]. Additionally, this is to date the closest a gubernatorial candidate has ever come to winning every single county in the state; Edgar lost [[Gallatin County, Illinois|Gallatin County]] by a mere 3 votes, less than 0.10%.{{cite web |title=1994 Gubernatorial General Election Data Graphs - Illinois |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/datagraph.php?year=1994&fips=17&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |publisher=US Election Atlas |access-date=13 July 2025}} Edgar won 70% of whites and 20% of African Americans.{{cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/1998/states/IL/polls/IL94GH.html|title=1994 ILLINOIS EXIT POLL RESULTS|website=[[CNN]]|date=1998|accessdate=17 September 2025}} ==Background== The primaries and general elections coincided with those for [[1994 United States House of Representatives elections#Illinois|Congress]], as well as those for other state offices. The election was part of the [[1994 Illinois elections]]. The 1994 [[midterm election]]s saw a strong showing by the Republican Party, which was dubbed the "[[Republican Revolution]]".
